title: Sarvam AI for Sahara: what to build and who could pay
decision: Use Sarvam for Indian-language care conversations, reviewed goals-of-care records and approved spoken explanations. Keep basic Sahara access free for patients and caregivers; sell the coordination workflow to care organisations.
scope: Research and proposed product direction. No Sarvam integration, account activation, patient upload, billing, email, release or deployment was performed for this research.

benefits.name: Sarvam AI sponsor credits
benefits.evidence: Health-a-thon Phase 2 update dated 13 October 2026 names Sarvam AI and says access instructions will follow.
benefits.confirmed: The provider is Sarvam AI, rather than Servo AI.
benefits.unknown: The sponsor allocation, redemption instructions, expiry, covered products, active balance and healthcare processing agreement are not established. No later access instructions were found in the connected email search.
benefits.nextUse: Once access is issued, first run fictional Hindi/English/Telugu conversations and produce reviewed educational audio. Establish the account's healthcare data terms before using identifiable patient conversations.

benefits.name: ChatGPT Pro
benefits.evidence: Health-a-thon offer dated 12 October 2026 promises one 30-day Pro subscription per team. A team reply is already present.
benefits.confirmed: The email promises a subscription benefit; activation was not verified.
benefits.unknown: It does not establish an OpenAI API allocation or an API budget for Sahara's users.
benefits.nextUse: After Pro redemption, use it for development, literature synthesis with source checking, test design, synthetic multilingual fixtures and review of product copy. Use the intended account and share work outputs; do not assume shared credentials or patient-data permissions.

mechanisms.name: Speech recognition
mechanisms.does: Converts audio into editable text; batch diarisation separates speaker labels.
mechanisms.doesNot: It does not know who a speaker is, validate a clinical statement or make a diagnosis.

mechanisms.name: Generative drafting
mechanisms.does: Organises supplied text into a draft, extracts supported fields and rewrites approved content.
mechanisms.doesNot: It does not supply a clinical evidence base, reliable citations or approved treatment by itself. Sahara must supply retrieval, validation and review.

mechanisms.name: Translation
mechanisms.does: Converts approved text between the selected supported languages.
mechanisms.doesNot: It does not guarantee preservation of clinical negation, numbers or medicine names. Check the exact language/model pair.

mechanisms.name: Speech synthesis
mechanisms.does: Reads an approved text aloud using a supported preset voice.
mechanisms.doesNot: Natural speech is not proof of a correct care plan. Use the approved version and make generated narration clear.

mechanisms.name: Document extraction
mechanisms.does: Converts a supplied document into text or candidate structured fields.
mechanisms.doesNot: It does not validate a prescription or justify changing a dose. Source image and clinician verification remain necessary.

mechanisms.name: Conversational orchestration
mechanisms.does: Combines recognition, generation, speech and permitted tools for a conversation.
mechanisms.doesNot: Bookings, authentication, verified directories, human handoff and actual writes still need a working service integration.

shortlist.title: A reviewed goals-of-care record from a conversation
shortlist.flow: Consent to record → capture the conversation → edit transcript and confirm speakers → draft supported goals, understanding, preferences, decisions and open questions → clinician approves → patient sees the same dated version.
shortlist.why: This is Sahara's distinctive core and reduces repeated explanations across visits.
shortlist.generativePart: Source-constrained structuring, with each material statement linked to its transcript excerpt and speaker.
shortlist.review: Do not infer treatment limits, capacity, prognosis, DNR status or legal directives. Unknown and disputed statements stay visible. Approval is versioned; a later change needs a new review.
shortlist.phase: Core clinical pilot after data agreement and clinician-led evaluation

shortlist.title: Listen to the approved plan
shortlist.flow: Open the clinician-approved plan → choose a tested language → listen, pause or replay a short section; keep the original text available.
shortlist.why: Useful when reading is tiring or the caregiver is more comfortable in another language.
shortlist.generativePart: Reviewed translation followed by speech synthesis; cache audio against the approved plan version.
shortlist.review: A bilingual clinical reviewer checks important numbers, medicine names and negation before patient-facing use. No invented expansion of instructions.
shortlist.phase: Start with approved general education; then personal plans after validation

shortlist.title: A voice diary that prepares the next visit
shortlist.flow: Speak a short update → confirm what was heard → save the dated note → create a source-linked visit brief and questions for the care team.
shortlist.why: Replaces a long form and helps families remember what changed.
shortlist.generativePart: Transcription, confirmed fact extraction and a chronological summary of the person's own reports.
shortlist.review: Label these entries patient-reported, separately from clinician-approved records. Do not turn self-reports into a diagnosis, predicted risk or a promise that a clinician is monitoring them. Display the agreed human contact route separately.
shortlist.phase: Early assisted-record pilot; Pood is only a prototype precedent

shortlist.title: A practical caregiver handover
shortlist.flow: Choose an approved care-plan version → dictate completed practical tasks and open questions → confirm owners → share a concise handover with permission.
shortlist.why: Reduces repeated calls when a different family member takes over.
shortlist.generativePart: Turns supported statements into a short, attributed checklist; read aloud if needed.
shortlist.review: Never silently assign medicines, alter administration instructions or identify the decision maker from a voice label. Real sharing requires authenticated roles and permission checks.

shortlist.title: Ask for care without completing another long form
shortlist.flow: Speak the location, language and access needs → confirm minimal details → search a maintained centre directory → show actual contact options and a draft enquiry.
shortlist.why: A clear support task that complements Sahara's MapLibre centres map.
shortlist.generativePart: Intent and location extraction, plain-language explanations and optionally spoken navigation.
shortlist.review: Availability, fees and bookings come from the service, not the model. Do not promise admission or send an enquiry without permission.

shortlist.title: Teach-back support for the nurse
shortlist.flow: Use an approved explanation → ask the person to describe it in their words → show a transcript beside the plan → nurse clarifies misunderstandings.
shortlist.why: Checks whether communication worked while preserving the human conversation.
shortlist.generativePart: Transcribe the response beside the approved explanation so the nurse can compare them. Automated highlighting of possible gaps is a later research option, requiring high-consequence omission and false-alarm evaluation.
shortlist.review: No pass/fail score for competence, consent or adherence; only a clinician can judge understanding and next steps.

architecture.currentApp: Keep the existing Kotlin / Jetpack Compose Android app, Room records and MapLibre centres. This research does not require a tech-stack change.
proposedFlow: Explicit recording control and participant consent
Authenticated backend job with a minimum required audio segment
Source-linked structured draft with no unsupported fields
Clinician review and a dated immutable approved version
Checked translation and Bulbul audio tied to that version
Patient acknowledgement and role-limited sharing with access history
architecture.backendWork: API credentials stay server-side. Build real authentication, file permissions, job state, cancellation, retry/deduplication, deletion and audit history. Room persistence alone does not establish care-team sync.
architecture.dataTerms: Sarvam's current terms apply a DPA for customer processing. They require professional involvement/review for tailored medical advice. The public privacy policy excludes enterprise content governed by customer agreements; it is not evidence of the exact retention, training or hosting terms for this account. Confirm those terms and healthcare scope before identifiable patient input.
architecture.localisation: Use the clinic's actual languages and test model/voice pairs. Do not advertise one uniform 22-language clinical voice experience; API coverage differs. Current docs recommend Saaras v4 and Bulbul v4-flash for new integrations, with v3 still relevant to some TTS languages.
architecture.currentScanner: Existing public photo scanning remains off. This research does not activate Sarvam, replace the scanner provider or change current release declarations.

validation.method: Use fictional consultations with code-switching, weak audio, overlapping speech, negation, names, numbers and corrections. Get bilingual clinical annotations; record critical errors, not just average word error.
Count unsupported statements, omitted preferences, wrong speaker attribution and incorrect certainty. A material uncorrected clinical error blocks that output from sharing.

Agree patient consent, participant roles, storage, retention and an escalation contact with a palliative partner. Compare current workflow with reviewed drafts; do not launch unattended medical advice.

Measure staff review minutes, correction burden, family plan retrieval, comprehension interviews, source traceability and completion of staff-assigned follow-up. Clinical benefit is not established by a faster transcript.
Measure actual minutes, characters, tokens and storage per active family. Cap retries, cache approved audio, retain manual entry and recover work when credits expire or the network fails.

funding.principle: Basic access for patients and caregivers stays free. A care organisation pays for the staff workflow and deployment; this is a proposed business model, not a customer commitment.

buyers.whatTheyBuy: Staff documentation, reviewed care-plan sharing, handovers, role permissions, audit history and integration/support.
buyers.priceStructure: Annual or monthly institution licence with a defined active-family/usage allowance; setup and integration scoped separately.
buyers.whyTheyMightPay: Less duplicate documentation and fewer communication gaps. Validate actual saved staff time and budget with buyers before setting a price.

buyers.who: Hospices, charitable hospitals and palliative NGOs
buyers.whatTheyBuy: Coordination for home-care teams and multilingual family communication, funded from an agreed project budget.
buyers.priceStructure: A partner or donor underwrites a capped cohort; the family does not buy a subscription.
buyers.whyTheyMightPay: Supports existing free services without adding a new patient fee.

buyers.who: Corporate CSR or philanthropic sponsors through an eligible care partner
buyers.whatTheyBuy: A defined deployment, training, support and an aggregate activity report with agreed privacy controls.
buyers.priceStructure: Time-limited project funding with a continuation plan. Do not assume a for-profit company can receive CSR grants as an eligible implementing agency.
buyers.whyTheyMightPay: Makes a specific free-care programme more accessible; Karunashraya publicly offers both free care and CSR participation.
buyers.stage: Partner-led funding hypothesis; eligibility and contract need checking

buyers.whatTheyBuy: An authorised palliative-care deployment, staff training, interoperability and programme support through the applicable procurement route.
buyers.priceStructure: State programme/procurement budget after a relevant pilot; not an automatic app reimbursement or open grant.
buyers.whyTheyMightPay: DGHS describes palliative-care proposals through state PIPs under NHM's Mission Flexipool. This is a policy fit, not evidence of a current Sahara tender or award.
buyers.stage: Later public-sector route, rather than the only possible payer

avoid: Charging families to read their own approved care record or access essential support
Referral commissions that bias which care service a family sees
Advertising against sensitive conversations or selling patient data
An unlimited voice-call promise priced only from expiring sponsor credits
funding.buyerDiscovery: Start with the assigned clinician/mentor and a palliative service lead. Ask who owns documentation, who reviews drafts, who has a software budget, which work takes time today, which languages matter and what a funded pilot must prove. No outreach was sent for this research.

costModel.label: Illustrative monthly provider spend for 100 active families; not a quote or a complete operating budget

lines.rate: Sarvam-105B ₹15/M input + ₹60/M output; no cache discount assumed
₹1/page for the extraction call; a separate digitisation call is not assumed

costModel.discrepancy: The live API documentation says ₹45/hour for diarisation, while the live marketing page says ₹0.59/minute (=₹35.40/hour). Standard STT is ₹30/hour vs ₹0.49/minute. This example uses the higher documented rate. Marketing lists Bulbul v4-flash at ₹2/1,000 characters, cheaper than v3, but model/language suitability and actual account billing must be checked.
costModel.excluded: GST or other tax treatment; hosting, storage, egress, telephony/WhatsApp/SMS, monitoring, support, clinical review, training, security work and integration. Managed Voice Agents have their own pricing and are not costed here. Character counts, tokenizer behaviour and retries affect actual usage.
costModel.interpretation: This is raw API arithmetic. It does not establish a sustainable selling price, a gross margin, care-team capacity, willingness to pay or a clinical outcome. The sponsor grant amount is not included.
